title: FARDC-Wazalendo Retake Mindjendje and Several Masisi Villages; Fighting Continues at Kasake
detail: Government forces and Wazalendo fighters confirmed recapture of the Mindjendje position in Walikale's Kisimba grouping on Wednesday, Sept 16, a day after launching the offensive that pushed AFC/M23 rebels back toward Malemo in Masisi; local sources described a precarious calm at Mindjendje by Sept 16, though the wider Kisimba grouping's security situation remained volatile. In Masisi's Ufamandu 1er grouping, the Wazalendo coalition recaptured several settlements — Remeka, Katuunda, Miko, Kareta and their surroundings — building on Sept 15's Miko hill recapture, with further positions recovered in Walikale's Luberike grouping and in the Katoyi and Osso-Banyungu sectors. Fresh fighting resumed early Wednesday around Kasake, a few kilometers from Remeka in the Bahunde chiefdom, involving roughly five Wazalendo groups allied with FARDC; a military spokesperson confirmed positions were reconquered in the area. Additional clashes were reported near Bibatama, Mitimingi and Katoyi-Centre. No casualty toll was available for any of the fronts, and many displaced families remained unable to return to their villages.

title: 17,755 Households Displaced in Walikale's Waloa Loanda Amid Masisi-Kalehe Fighting
detail: Local authorities reported Sept 16 that 17,755 households have been displaced into the Waloa Loanda grouping of Walikale territory, North Kivu, sheltering across six villages — Biriko, Busurungi, Lukaraba, Manje, Myanga and Malembe — after fleeing armed confrontations between AFC/M23 and FARDC-Wazalendo forces in Masisi and Kalehe territories since August 2026. Local chief Mwami Asili Mafuluko said displaced families are surviving mainly on solidarity from host families who are themselves affected, and appealed for urgent assistance. The Itebero health zone reported medication shortages across facilities, with no active humanitarian partners currently providing support to the area.

title: FARDC Says It Neutralized Four Suspected Rwandan Special Forces in Fizi Highlands; 14 M23-Twirwaneho Fighters Surrender
detail: FARDC's Sukola 2 operations sector said a counter-operation between Mulima and Mukoko in the Fizi territory highlands, South Kivu, on Sept 15 neutralized four individuals it identified as Rwandan (RDF) special forces, with military equipment recovered from the site, according to spokesperson Sub-Lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji. Separately, FARDC reported that 14 combatants affiliated with AFC/M23 and its ally Twirwaneho — including a former FARDC soldier, arriving notably from Rugezi and Mukoko — surrendered and laid down their weapons in the same period, and were taken into the army's care. The military renewed its call for remaining armed group members to disarm and join regular FARDC units. Neither Rwanda nor M23 issued a public response to the RDF neutralization claim.

title: DRC-Rwanda JSCM Talks Open in Geneva for Second Day Amid Renewed Eastern DRC Fighting
detail: DRC and Rwandan delegations reconvened in Geneva on Sept 16 for the seventh Joint Security Coordination Mechanism (JSCM) meeting under the Washington Accords, running through Sept 17 with mediators from the US, Qatar, Togo and the African Union Commission. The session follows the Aug 12-13 sixth JSCM meeting, at which the two sides agreed to advance two monitoring and verification initiatives now awaiting US feedback, and is meant to feed into an October trilateral planning conference. FDLR neutralization remains the central unresolved obligation: the DRC's July 28 disarmament protocol with an FDLR faction has drawn Rwandan rejection, with Kigali insisting on neutralization rather than negotiated disarmament and conditioning its own defensive-posture rollback on the group's dismantlement. The talks opened as fighting continued in North Kivu's Masisi and Walikale territories and South Kivu's Fizi highlands, underscoring the gap between the diplomatic track and conditions on the ground.
